questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: A multipara at term has a transverse lie with the fetal back anterior and membranes intact, and the cervix is 2 cm dilated. The correct management is:
questions.concept: A persistent transverse lie at term cannot deliver vaginally and risks cord prolapse and uterine rupture once membranes rupture, so delivery is by caesarean; internal podalic version is confined to the second twin.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: On vaginal examination in labour the anterior fontanelle is felt centrally with the sagittal suture transverse. This indicates:
options: Deep transverse arrest with a deflexed head
questions.concept: Feeling the anterior fontanelle centrally means the head is deflexed rather than well flexed, and a sagittal suture lying transverse at the level of the ischial spines with no progress defines deep transverse arrest.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: A woman in obstructed labour has a temperature of 39 degrees, a pulse of 130 and offensive liquor after 20 hours of labour at home. The most urgent priority alongside delivery is:
options: Antibiotics and fluid resuscitation before operative intervention
questions.concept: Obstructed labour with sepsis and dehydration carries high maternal mortality, so resuscitation and broad-spectrum antibiotics run concurrently with arranging caesarean delivery.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: A primigravida at term has a mento-posterior face presentation with no descent after 2 hours of good contractions. The appropriate management is:
questions.concept: A persistent mento-posterior face cannot deliver vaginally because the fetal neck is already maximally extended and cannot extend further to negotiate the pelvic curve, unlike a mento-anterior face which can deliver by flexion.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: In a brow presentation at term, which engaging diameter makes vaginal delivery of a normal-sized fetus impossible?
questions.concept: The mento-vertical diameter is the largest anteroposterior diameter of the fetal head, so a persistent brow must either convert to a face or a vertex or be delivered by caesarean.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: A woman with a previous caesarean scar in labour develops sudden severe abdominal pain, cessation of contractions, fetal bradycardia and a rising maternal pulse with vaginal bleeding. The diagnosis is:
questions.concept: Loss of contractions with an abnormally palpable fetal presenting part, maternal tachycardia and acute fetal distress in a scarred uterus indicates rupture, requiring immediate laparotomy.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: A short primigravida has a fetus with an estimated weight of 3.8 kg and the head remains high with a poorly applied cervix after 3 hours in the active phase. This picture suggests:
questions.concept: Failure of descent with a high head and a poorly applied cervix despite adequate contractions in a small woman with a large fetus indicates disproportion, and trial of labour must be abandoned rather than augmented.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: Which manoeuvre is contraindicated in shoulder dystocia because it worsens impaction?
questions.concept: Fundal pressure drives the anterior shoulder harder against the symphysis and increases the risk of uterine rupture and brachial plexus injury; suprapubic pressure directed obliquely is the correct adjunct.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: In a locked twin where the first twin is breech and the second cephalic, the heads impact at the pelvic brim. The correct management is:
options: Vigorous traction on the first twin
Destructive operation on the second twin
questions.concept: Locking is a rare obstetric emergency in which neither twin can descend; caesarean delivery is the safe modern approach, and vigorous traction risks decapitation and uterine rupture.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abnormal labour: malpresentation, obstructed labour, CPD
questions.stem: A woman with untreated obstructed labour delivers and 7 days later develops continuous urinary leakage with a normal bladder capacity. The most likely lesion is:
questions.concept: Prolonged impaction of the head compresses the bladder base against the symphysis, and the resulting ischaemic slough separates around the seventh to tenth day, producing a fistula rather than immediate leakage.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abnormal Labour

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, recurrent pregnancy loss
questions.stem: A woman at 9 weeks has vaginal bleeding with a closed cervical os, and ultrasound shows a live fetus of appropriate size. The diagnosis is:
questions.concept: Bleeding with a closed os and a viable intrauterine pregnancy defines threatened abortion, and about two-thirds continue to term with expectant management.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abortion and Ectopic Pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, recurrent pregnancy loss
questions.stem: A woman with an intrauterine pregnancy of 10 weeks by dates has an ultrasound showing a gestational sac of 30 mm with no embryo. This indicates:
questions.concept: A mean sac diameter of 25 mm or more with no embryo meets the criterion for early pregnancy failure, and medical or surgical evacuation is then offered.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abortion and Ectopic Pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, recurrent pregnancy loss
questions.stem: A stable woman has a 2 cm unruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy, a beta-hCG of 1800 IU/L, no fetal cardiac activity and no free fluid. Methotrexate is chosen. Which follow-up finding indicates treatment success?
options: A fall in beta-hCG of at least 15 percent between days 4 and 7
Any fall in beta-hCG by day 2
Disappearance of the mass on day 7 ultrasound
questions.concept: Beta-hCG characteristically rises between day 1 and day 4 before falling, so the day 4 to day 7 comparison is the accepted measure; separation pain around day 3 is expected and is not failure.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abortion and Ectopic Pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, recurrent pregnancy loss
questions.stem: Which finding is an absolute contraindication to medical management of an ectopic pregnancy with methotrexate?
questions.concept: Rupture with instability demands immediate surgery; other relative contraindications include cardiac activity in the ectopic, a mass above 4 cm and a beta-hCG above 5000 IU/L.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abortion and Ectopic Pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, recurrent pregnancy loss
questions.stem: A woman with three consecutive first-trimester losses has a normal karyotype in both partners and a normal uterine cavity, but the lupus anticoagulant is positive on two occasions 12 weeks apart. The treatment that improves live birth rate is:
options: Low-dose aspirin with low molecular weight heparin from confirmation of pregnancy
questions.concept: Antiphospholipid syndrome is the only clearly treatable cause of recurrent miscarriage, and combined aspirin and heparin raises live birth rates substantially.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abortion and Ectopic Pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, recurrent pregnancy loss
questions.stem: A woman presents with a mid-trimester loss preceded by painless cervical dilatation and bulging membranes, having had a similar loss previously. The management in a future pregnancy is:
options: History-indicated cervical cerclage at 12 to 14 weeks
questions.concept: Cervical insufficiency causes painless dilatation without contractions, and a prophylactic cerclage placed early in the next pregnancy, with progesterone if the cervix shortens, is the accepted approach.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abortion and Ectopic Pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, recurrent pregnancy loss
questions.stem: Uterine evacuation for a second-trimester missed abortion is complicated by sudden collapse with bleeding from puncture sites. The likely diagnosis is:
options: Disseminated intravascular coagulation from a retained dead fetus
questions.concept: Thromboplastins released from a fetus retained beyond about four weeks consume clotting factors, so coagulation should be checked before evacuating a long-standing missed abortion.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abortion and Ectopic Pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Abortion, ectopic pregnancy, recurrent pregnancy loss
questions.stem: Which uterine anomaly carries the highest risk of mid-trimester loss and is amenable to hysteroscopic correction?
questions.concept: The poorly vascularised fibromuscular septum implants badly, and hysteroscopic septal resection improves outcomes, whereas a bicornuate uterus requires abdominal metroplasty and an arcuate uterus is a normal variant.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Abortion and Ectopic Pregnancy

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Ca cervix / endometrium / ovary; screening
questions.stem: A woman with cervical carcinoma has disease extending to the lower third of the vagina but no pelvic wall involvement and normal hydronephrosis-free kidneys. Her FIGO stage is:
questions.concept: Lower-third vaginal involvement defines stage IIIA, extension to the pelvic side wall or hydronephrosis defines IIIB, and bladder or rectal mucosal invasion defines IVA.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Genital Malignancies

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Ca cervix / endometrium / ovary; screening
questions.stem: Which histological type of cervical carcinoma is least reliably detected by cytology-based screening?
options: Adenocarcinoma arising in the endocervical canal
questions.concept: Endocervical adenocarcinoma arises high in the canal beyond the reach of the spatula and lacks a well-defined precursor lesion, which is one reason HPV-based screening has improved detection.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Genital Malignancies

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Ca cervix / endometrium / ovary; screening
questions.stem: A 62-year-old woman has grade 1 endometrioid adenocarcinoma confined to the endometrium on hysteroscopic biopsy. The standard primary treatment is:
options: Total hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and surgical staging
Radical hysterectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy in all cases
questions.concept: Endometrial cancer is staged surgically, and even early disease requires removal of the ovaries because they are a site of occult spread and of continuing oestrogen production.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Genital Malignancies

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Ca cervix / endometrium / ovary; screening
questions.stem: Which ovarian tumour marker is most useful for monitoring a young woman treated for a dysgerminoma?
questions.concept: Dysgerminoma characteristically secretes lactate dehydrogenase and sometimes placental alkaline phosphatase, whereas alpha-fetoprotein marks yolk sac tumour and CA-125 epithelial disease.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Genital Malignancies

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Ca cervix / endometrium / ovary; screening
questions.stem: A postmenopausal woman has a 6 cm complex ovarian cyst with solid areas, ascites and a raised CA-125. The most appropriate next step is:
options: Referral to a gynaecological oncology centre for staging laparotomy
Aspiration of the cyst under ultrasound
questions.concept: A high risk of malignancy index warrants primary surgery by a subspecialist because complete staging and optimal debulking determine survival, and cyst aspiration risks spilling malignant cells.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Genital Malignancies

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Ca cervix / endometrium / ovary; screening
questions.stem: Which criterion in cervical carcinoma makes primary chemoradiation preferable to radical hysterectomy?
options: Involvement of the parametrium (stage IIB or above)
questions.concept: Once the parametrium is involved, surgery cannot achieve clear margins and combining it with radiotherapy compounds morbidity, so concurrent cisplatin-based chemoradiation becomes the treatment of choice.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Genital Malignancies

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Ca cervix / endometrium / ovary; screening
questions.stem: A woman with a granulosa cell tumour of the ovary requires which additional endometrial assessment?
options: Endometrial sampling, because oestrogen secretion causes hyperplasia or carcinoma
Screening for a germline BRCA mutation
questions.concept: Granulosa cell tumours secrete oestrogen and inhibin, so up to a quarter have coexisting endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma, and inhibin is used for long-term surveillance given the risk of very late recurrence.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Genital Malignancies

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Contraception
questions.stem: A woman has a copper intrauterine device in situ and a positive pregnancy test with an intrauterine gestation she wishes to continue. The correct action is:
options: Remove the device if the threads are visible
Leave the device and give antibiotics
Push the device higher into the fundus
questions.concept: Leaving a device in place raises the risk of second-trimester loss, chorioamnionitis and preterm birth, so removal is advised when the threads are accessible.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Contraception

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Contraception
questions.stem: Which contraceptive method reduces the risk of both endometrial and ovarian carcinoma with increasing duration of use?
questions.concept: Suppression of ovulation and of endometrial proliferation gives roughly a 50 percent reduction in ovarian and endometrial cancer that persists for years after stopping, a key counselling point balanced against thrombotic risk.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Contraception

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Contraception
questions.stem: A woman using the progestogen-only pill misses a tablet by 5 hours. The advice is:
options: Take it at once and use additional precautions for 48 hours
Stop the pill and start a new pack after the next period
questions.concept: Traditional progestogen-only pills have only a 3-hour window, so a delay beyond that requires backup contraception; the desogestrel formulation allows a 12-hour window.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Contraception

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Contraception
questions.stem: Which finding on counselling would make the levonorgestrel intrauterine system the preferred method?
options: Heavy menstrual bleeding with a desire for contraception
Desire for immediate return of fertility after removal
questions.concept: The system reduces menstrual blood loss by up to 90 percent and is licensed for menorrhagia and endometrial protection, so it addresses two problems at once.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Contraception

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Contraception
questions.stem: After medical abortion at 8 weeks, when can a combined oral contraceptive pill be started?
options: Immediately, on the day of the procedure
After a negative pregnancy test at 6 weeks
questions.concept: Ovulation can occur within 2 to 3 weeks of abortion, so immediate initiation gives no additional risk and avoids the high rate of rapid repeat pregnancy seen with delayed starts.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Contraception

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Contraception
questions.stem: Which mechanism explains why the copper intrauterine device is effective as emergency contraception up to 5 days after ovulation is expected?
options: Copper ions are toxic to sperm and the sterile inflammatory reaction prevents implantation
It blocks the luteinising hormone surge
questions.concept: Because its action includes an anti-implantation effect, the copper device works even after the fertile window has passed and is the most effective emergency method with a failure rate below 1 in 1000.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Contraception

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: A woman with an uncertain last menstrual period has a first-trimester scan showing a crown-rump length of 45 mm. This corresponds to a gestational age of about:
questions.concept: Crown-rump length dating between 7 and 13 weeks is accurate to within 5 days, and a length of about 45 mm corresponds to 11 weeks; after 14 weeks biparietal diameter and femur length are used instead.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: Which ultrasound soft marker in the second trimester is most strongly associated with trisomy 21?
questions.concept: Nasal bone hypoplasia carries the highest likelihood ratio among second-trimester soft markers, whereas isolated choroid plexus cysts and mild pyelectasis have little independent significance.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: A cardiotocograph shows a baseline of 140, variability of 4 beats per minute over 60 minutes and no accelerations. This indicates:
options: Reduced variability requiring further assessment for fetal hypoxia or sedation
questions.concept: Variability below 5 beats for more than 40 minutes is the single most important marker of impaired central autonomic control, though sleep cycles and maternal opioids or magnesium can cause it transiently.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: A growth-restricted fetus at 32 weeks has absent end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery but a normal ductus venosus and normal computerised short-term variation. The management is:
options: Intensive surveillance with corticosteroids and planned delivery, usually by 34 weeks
questions.concept: Absent end-diastolic flow indicates advanced placental insufficiency but with normal venous Doppler there is time to give steroids; reversed flow or abnormal ductus venosus mandates prompt delivery.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: Which Doppler parameter best predicts fetal anaemia in red cell alloimmunisation?
options: Middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity
questions.concept: Anaemia lowers blood viscosity and raises cardiac output, increasing peak systolic velocity in the middle cerebral artery, and a value above 1.5 multiples of the median predicts moderate to severe anaemia.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: First-trimester combined screening for aneuploidy uses nuchal translucency together with which biochemical markers?
options: Free beta-hCG and pregnancy-associated plasma protein A
questions.concept: In trisomy 21 pregnancy-associated plasma protein A is low and free beta-hCG high; the quadruple test with alpha-fetoprotein, oestriol, hCG and inhibin A belongs to the second trimester.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: A woman at 41 weeks has a modified biophysical profile with a non-reactive non-stress test and an amniotic fluid index of 3 cm. The appropriate action is:
options: Delivery, as oligohydramnios with a non-reactive trace indicates chronic placental insufficiency
questions.concept: Amniotic fluid volume reflects chronic fetal renal perfusion and falls with sustained hypoxaemia, so its reduction with an abnormal trace is an indication to deliver.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: Cell-free fetal DNA screening returns a high-risk result for trisomy 21. The correct counselling is:
options: Confirmatory invasive testing by amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling is required before any irreversible decision
The result is diagnostic and termination can be offered directly
No further action is needed if the scan is normal
questions.concept: Cell-free DNA is a screening test with a high but not perfect positive predictive value, which varies with prevalence, and false positives occur from confined placental mosaicism, vanishing twin and maternal malignancy.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Diagnosis of pregnancy, antenatal imaging & fetal surveillance
questions.stem: Which finding on a cardiotocograph is most specific for fetal anaemia or acute severe hypoxia?
options: A sinusoidal pattern with a regular smooth undulation of 3 to 5 cycles per minute
questions.concept: A true sinusoidal pattern lasting more than 10 minutes is rare and ominous, classically seen in fetomaternal haemorrhage, severe alloimmune anaemia and ruptured vasa praevia.
questions.reference: DC Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics 9e, Ch. Antenatal Assessment

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: Which symptom pattern is most characteristic of deep infiltrating endometriosis of the rectovaginal septum?
options: Deep dyspareunia with cyclical dyschezia and painful defaecation during menstruation
questions.concept: Nodules in the rectovaginal septum and uterosacral ligaments are stretched during intercourse and defaecation, and the cyclical timing follows the hormonal responsiveness of the ectopic endometrium.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: The definitive diagnosis of peritoneal endometriosis requires:
options: Response to a therapeutic trial of oral contraceptives
questions.concept: Ultrasound reliably detects endometriomas and deep disease but not superficial peritoneal implants, and CA-125 is neither sensitive nor specific, so laparoscopy remains the reference standard.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: Which pathological feature distinguishes adenomyosis from endometriosis?
options: Endometrial glands and stroma within the myometrium
questions.concept: Adenomyosis is the presence of endometrial tissue deep within the myometrium with surrounding smooth muscle hyperplasia, producing a diffusely bulky tender uterus rather than discrete pelvic implants.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: A 32-year-old with endometriosis-associated pain wishes to conceive within a year. Which treatment is appropriate?
options: Laparoscopic excision or ablation of endometriosis, which improves both pain and fecundity
questions.concept: All medical treatments for endometriosis are contraceptive, so in a woman seeking pregnancy surgical treatment of the disease is the option that addresses pain and subfertility together.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: A gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist is used for 6 months for endometriosis. Add-back therapy is given to:
options: Prevent bone mineral density loss and vasomotor symptoms from hypo-oestrogenism
questions.concept: Low-dose oestrogen with a progestogen protects bone and relieves menopausal symptoms without abolishing the therapeutic suppression, which allows treatment beyond 6 months.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: Which imaging finding on transvaginal ultrasound suggests adenomyosis rather than a fibroid?
options: An indistinct junctional zone with myometrial cysts and a globular uterus
A well-defined hypoechoic mass with peripheral vascularity
questions.concept: Fibroids are discrete and capsulated with rim vascularity, whereas adenomyosis diffusely thickens and heterogeneously distorts the myometrium with small cystic spaces and no clear plane.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: A woman with a 5 cm ovarian endometrioma is undergoing surgery before assisted reproduction. Which technique best preserves ovarian reserve?
options: Careful cystectomy with stripping of the capsule, minimising thermal energy near the hilum
Extensive bipolar coagulation of the cyst bed
questions.concept: Endometriomas lack a true capsule so stripping removes some normal cortex, and excessive coagulation destroys follicles, which is why anti-Mullerian hormone falls after surgery and technique matters.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: Which theory best explains endometriosis occurring at sites remote from the pelvis such as the pleura?
options: Lymphatic and haematogenous dissemination of endometrial cells
questions.concept: Retrograde menstruation explains the pelvic distribution, but thoracic and even cerebral endometriosis require vascular or lymphatic spread, which is why several theories coexist rather than one explaining all cases.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
questions.topic: Endometriosis, adenomyosis & chronic pelvic pain
questions.stem: A woman with chronic pelvic pain has a normal laparoscopy. Which condition should be actively considered?
options: Pelvic floor myofascial pain and central sensitisation, often with coexisting bladder or bowel symptoms
questions.concept: Up to a third of women with chronic pelvic pain have a normal laparoscopy, and the pain is then usually musculoskeletal or neuropathic with central amplification, so repeated surgery is unhelpful and multidisciplinary management is needed.
questions.reference: Shaw's Textbook of Gynaecology 17e, Ch. Endometriosis
